sections.title: Why adhesive-label, plastic-housed and snap-fit RFID tags fail in industrial chemical environments
bullets: Plastic-housed RFID tags (ABS / PC / PVC / PA) crack, yellow, chalk and become brittle after 6-18 months of outdoor UV exposure per ASTM G154 QUV Cycle 1 + ISO 4892-2 accelerated-weathering. Refineries + chemical plants + offshore platforms disqualify <5-year tag-life architectures at asset-integrity-management (AIM) audit.

Adhesive-backed labels (3M 7613T / 7874T / 7871) lose bond on surfaces contaminated with oil, grease, paint-overspray or chemical-residue. Surface-energy drops below the wetting threshold of typical 38-42 dyne/cm acrylic adhesives, driving label-detachment rates of 3-8 % per year on industrial equipment.

Tags with ultrasonic-welded or snap-fit housings allow progressive moisture ingress through the seam over 12-36 months — hydrolysis of internal bond-wires + antenna etch drives gradual read-rate degradation from 99 % to <80 % before outright failure.

High-temperature environments above 100 °C (steam-trap + autoclave + engine-bay + exhaust-adjacent) exceed the rating of standard tag housings + acrylic adhesives. ABS / PC melt above 150-180 °C; 3M VHB 4941 holds 149 °C continuous but loses bond above 232 °C long-term.

Hazardous-area installations in Class I Div 1 / 2 gas + Class II Div 1 / 2 dust per NFPA 70 NEC Article 500 require encapsulation per IEC 60079-18 Ex m. Standard plastic-housed tags are not ATEX / IECEx approved and are non-compliant for zone-rated installations.

faq.question: What chemicals can the epoxy tag withstand?
faq.answer: The industrial-grade two-part DGEBA + amine-cured epoxy resin resists continuous exposure per ASTM D543 chemical-resistance classification: aliphatic + aromatic hydrocarbons (gasoline + diesel + jet-A + toluene + xylene), alcohols (IPA + ethanol + methanol), ketones (acetone + MEK short-term only), 10 % HCl, 20 % H₂SO₄, 30 % NaOH + 10 % NH₄OH, brake-fluid DOT-4/5.1, lubricating oils + transmission fluids, CIP detergents + enzymatic cleaners. The silica-filled anhydride-cured high-temp variant extends resistance to concentrated acids + bases + aggressive solvents for petrochemical service. Share your specific chemical-exposure profile (chemistry + concentration + temperature + immersion / splash / wipe + duration / frequency) for a validated ASTM D543 material-selection recommendation.

faq.question: Is the epoxy tag ATEX + IECEx + UL hazardous-area approved?
faq.answer: Yes. The Proud Tek epoxy tag qualifies under ATEX Directive 2014/34/EU Ex m encapsulated protection + IECEx Scheme IEC 60079-18 (Equipment protection by encapsulation 'm') + UL 913 Intrinsic Safety + UL 121201 Nonincendive + NFPA 70 NEC Article 500 Class I Div 1 / 2 (gas) + Class II Div 1 / 2 (dust) + CEC Section 18. Applications include Zone 1 / 21 gas + dust hazardous installations in refineries, chemical plants, offshore platforms + fuel-handling facilities. The encapsulation compound is the approved barrier preventing ignition of surrounding explosive atmospheres. Declaration of conformity + coverage letter + material-declaration per RoHS 3 + REACH SVHC + IEC 62474 supplied per order.

faq.question: Can the epoxy tag be used on metal?
faq.answer: Yes. Two variants are offered: (1) on-metal tuned with embedded ferrite isolation layer (25 × 5 mm disc or 50 × 30 × 4 mm plaque) delivering 1-3 m UHF read-range on steel / aluminium / stainless / cast-iron without spacer foam, and (2) standard off-metal for non-metallic mounting (plastic + glass + composite + painted / powder-coated surfaces) with 3-6 m UHF range. Specify on-metal when ordering if mounting is metallic — the ferrite isolation layer prevents antenna-to-metal detuning that otherwise collapses read-range to 10-30 cm on a standard off-metal tag.

faq.question: How is the tag attached to the asset?
faq.answer: Primary method: industrial-grade 3M VHB 5952 (260 °C peak / 149 °C continuous) or 3M VHB 4941 general-purpose acrylic structural adhesive — bond strength 15-25 N/cm² on clean / dry / surface-prepared substrate. Secondary method: mechanical M3 / M4 cap-screw + Nyloc locknut or pop-rivet through mounting-hole for mission-critical retention. Tertiary method: ATEX hazardous-area variant uses 316L stainless back-plate + M6 stud-weld + high-temp two-part epoxy mounting-cement (Aremco Duralco 4460 / Loctite EA 9340) for 200 °C + permanent retention. Surface preparation critical per 3M application-bulletin: clean to ≥38 dyne/cm wetting energy + isopropyl-alcohol degrease + 24-h cure at ambient.
